title: Lesson 6: Sharing Jesus with Others
description: Something amazing just happened in your life, and the most natural thing in the world is to tell someone. Like the woman at the well, you do not need training to say "come and see." This lesson gives you a first taste of the BLESS rhythm and points back to the ABCs for the gospel itself.

blocks.text: Tell Someone What Just Happened

In the last lesson you saw that God saved you into a family. Now He wants to use you to invite others in. You have been rescued, forgiven, and adopted, and the most natural response is to tell someone. Evangelism is not a sales pitch or a program. It is one beggar telling another beggar where to find bread. Before any how-to, watch how it happened for one woman.

blocks.alt: Jesus speaking with the Samaritan woman at the well

blocks.title: The Woman at the Well
blocks.text:
Jesus once stopped at a well and struck up a conversation with a Samaritan woman who had every reason to avoid people. She had a complicated past, she was from a people most Jews looked down on, and she had come to draw water at noon, in the heat of the day (John 4:6). Jesus talked to her anyway, and what happened next is one of the most spontaneous moments of evangelism in the Bible.

"So the woman left her water jar and went away into town and said to the people, 'Come, see a man who told me all that I ever did. Can this be the Christ?'" (John 4:28-29)

She left her water jar, ran back into the town she had been hiding from, and told everyone. No training, no program, no polished presentation, just a woman who had met Jesus and could not keep it to herself. She said, "Come and see."

Notice the order. Jesus came to her first. He crossed the distance, started the conversation, and offered her living water before she ever told a soul. You share Jesus for the same reason she did: because He found you first. You do not have to be an expert to share Jesus. You only have to say "come and see" and tell what He did for you.
6.1 - Who did God use to bring you to faith, and what did they do?
blocks.data_question: 6.1 - Who God used to bring you to faith

blocks.text: Your Personal Ministry

Your personal ministry is sharing the good news with people you know and people you meet, so they too can know Jesus. Successful evangelism is simply sharing the good news; it does not depend on the person's response. The results belong to God.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
A First Taste of BLESS

A simple rhythm called BLESS helps you live on mission every day, and if you look at the well again you will see Jesus doing almost all of it. Growing Out, the 203 course, walks through each rhythm in full. Tap through below for a first taste.
6.2 - List three people who can be a part of your personal ministry inviting to "Come and See" what Jesus has done in your life and also you can start to BLESS.
6.3 - What are some actions you can take with these people you just wrote down in question 6.2?
blocks.data_question: 6.3 - Ways to care for those who do not follow Jesus

blocks.text: Story: Say What Happened to You

The woman at the well did not give a sermon. She told her story, and you already have one. You met Jesus. Start there. When the moment comes to explain the gospel itself, use the ABCs you learned in Lesson 2: Admit you are a sinner and need a Savior (Romans 3:23), Believe in Jesus, His death and resurrection (Romans 10:9), and Confess Jesus as your Lord (Romans 10:9). The full picture of sharing your story and the gospel comes in Growing Out, Lesson 5.

How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, "How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!"

Those beautiful feet belong to ordinary people who have been loved by God and want to share it with others. Fear is normal; the woman at the well had plenty to be worried about. Remember that Jesus did not send her out trained. He sent her out known by God.
6.4 - What is motivating you to share your faith right now, and what are the things that might be holding you back?
This Week's Practice

Pray each day for the three people you listed. Then, before the week ends, tell one of them in two or three sentences what Jesus has done for you, and leave the door open with the woman's four words: come and see.
Lesson 6 Review

You do not have to be an expert to share Jesus. You only have to tell what He did for you and point people to Him. The woman at the well did not wait until she had all the answers; she went, because Jesus had found her first. BLESS gives you a simple way to love the people already around you, and the ABCs give you words when it is time to share the gospel. Come and see is still the whole invitation.
In the next lesson, you will learn what to do when you drift, and how the Shepherd comes looking for you.

blocks.heading: Introduction to John 16, 17, and 18
blocks.intro: In John 16, 17, 18, Jesus prepares His disciples for what is coming, prays for everyone who will ever believe in Him, including you, and is then arrested and put on trial. As you read, notice what it looks like to stand for Jesus when the pressure is on.

blocks.text: Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What have you learned about God and yourself recently in your Daily Devotions?
What is a prayer request for this week?

The BLESS rhythms are adapted from BLESS: 5 Everyday Ways to Love Your Neighbor and Change the World by Dave Ferguson and Jon Ferguson. The picture of one beggar telling another where to find bread comes from D. T. Niles.
